# Format-Limited KML Case

A KML file demonstrating inherent format limitations: all extended-data attributes are stored as strings regardless of their original type, coordinates are always WGS 84, and Z coordinates are included even when not meaningful. Exposes loaders or converters that assume numeric attribute types survive a KML round-trip.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Case ID | `format_limited_kml_case` |
| Category | vector |
| Format | KML |
| Geometry type | Polygon |
| CRS | `EPSG:4326` |
| Test tier | unit |
| Size class | tiny |
| Storage class | bundled |
| Redistributable | yes |
| Loader | `geopandas` |
| Status | validated |

## Use this case

```python
import pytest


@pytest.mark.geocase_case("format_limited_kml_case")
def test_format_limited_kml_case(geocase_case) -> None:
    data = geocase_case.load()
    assert data is not None
```

## What this case checks

Detect loaders or cross-format converters that assume attribute types (integer, float, boolean) survive a KML round-trip. In KML all ExtendedData SimpleField values are strings, so population "15000" is a string, not an int. Naive downstream code that does arithmetic on these columns without casting will fail silently.
